_comment: THE DEFAULT FLOOR TYPE -- what a hole in a house's foundation opens into. A floor type is the whole recipe for a kind of space: its shape, its look, which holes it can grow, and how far sideways it runs. Other types name this one as their base and override only what differs (RFC 7386 merge), so retuning the shared shape happens once. tile_size 32 against the 1280x720 internal render gives 40x22 tiles on screen -- the close, room-at-a-time framing this game wants -- while the buffer still upscales by a clean integer. Chunkiness comes from the TILE, not from starving the framebuffer. SIZE: a dug chamber is one fight, not a level -- about two screens across, so the swarm finds you rather than you hunting it through empty corridor. rooms lists the template pools this type draws from, shared first. spaced_markers: placement rules for marker letters that are SPAWNERS -- they keep a minimum distance from the spawn (nobody should surface next to the way in) and from each other; a marker violating the rule is dropped, but a floor always keeps at least one (the farthest from the spawn), because a chamber with nothing seeping is not a chamber. seep_types: what kinds of hole this floor can open -- one is rolled per spawner marker, deterministically from the floor's seed, so a layout is the same holes every time. marker_seeps pins a letter to a kind: an authored room can say THIS spot is a gnawed gap; plain P still rolls. wall_depth is how many tiles of solid a wall needs behind its face before a hole may be gnawed through it -- one tile is a partition with the same room on its other side, and a hole through that leads nowhere, which is why they must not appear on the stubs of wall standing inside a room. max_rooms is how many rooms this kind of space may hold at ONE DEPTH, counted across every way down that reaches it. A floor at a full depth simply grows no more holes in walls -- they fall back to holes in the ground the same way one with no wall to arch into does -- so a run sideways expands outward from where he first came down and then stops, without anything ever refusing a hole that is already drawn.
